text.p: STOCKS GOLD
Dow Jones close Latest spot rate
FTSE-100 close CRUDE OIL
Nikkei-225 latest $23.10 per bbl
Stocks broke more records Wednesday amid gains in technology shares and a surge in bonds.
The dollar rose above 112 Japanese yen for the first time since January 1994, as Japanese investors continued to reject the skimpy yields of yen-denominated investments.

"The market keeps chugging ahead. The driving force is the market has been basically moving higher every year for six years and it's fairly magnetic to investors," said Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 29.07 to 5,933.97, handily topping Tuesday's record close of 5,904.90. In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced decliners by 1,630 to 762 with 439 million shares traded on the New York Stock Exchange.
After closing above 5,900 for the first time Tuesday, "we're reaching for the 6,000 mark. At this rate, we can get there by the end of the week," said Ken Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage.

The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks notched its third consecutive all-time high finish, up 4.93 to 694.01. The NYSE Composite index posted its fifth straight record, up 2.36 to 370.54. The average price per share rose 25 cents.

The technology-rich Nasdaq Composite index, which shed 8.54 points over the past two sessions, rallied 14.60 to 1,236.11. That drew the index closer to its record closing high of 1,249.15, set June 5.

Stocks were supported by continued strength in the bond market. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose nearly half a point, knocking its yield down to 6.84 percent -- the lowest since Aug. 22 -- from 6.88 percent at Tuesday's close.
A growing conviction that long term interest rates will stay below 7 percent in the near term and that corporate profits will not be hurt by higher rates, are luring investors.

The dollar settled at 111.87 yen in late trading, up from 111.43 yen late Tuesday. The dollar rose to 1.5325 German marks, its best performance since June 25, when it reached 1.5350. The dollar closed at 1.5263 marks Tuesday.
Heating oil prices reached a 5-1/2 year high at the New York Mercantile Exchange on reports of low supplies in the northeastern United States.

Spot heating oil prices peaked at 73.15 cents a gallon Wednesday, the highest since 74.40 set late in January 1991. Heating oil futures for November delivery settled 1.22 cents higher at 71.98 cents a gallon after peaking at 73.15.

Gasoline prices tumbled at NYMEX, pulling crude oil down after the same industry reports showed supplies were building. November crude settled 9 cents lower at $24.05 a barrel, and November gasoline settled 0.40 cent lower at 62.42 cents a gallon.
Actively traded December cotton rose 1.59 cents to 77.75 cents per pound on crop problems in Texas and the former Soviet Union.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 closed above 4,000 for the first time, gaining 22.9 points to end at 4,015.1. In Tokyo, the 225-issue Nikkei average closed 35.63 points or 0.17 percent higher at 21,498.60.
